scheme_name: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme For BPL Families Belonging To Scheduled Caste (SC) Category
description:
The Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme for Below Poverty Line (BPL) Families Belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) Category was launched by the Government of India on 1st April 2021. 

This scheme aims to provide nutritional support to pregnant indigenous cows and buffaloes owned by BPL families who belong to the SC category. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the health and productivity of indigenous livestock. 

The scheme also aims to empower SC families by providing them with financial assistance to maintain their livestock. 

The targeted beneficiaries of this scheme are BPL families that belong to the Scheduled Caste category. 

To qualify for this scheme, the family must be listed under the BPL category as per the latest socio-economic census. 

Additionally, the family must own at least one pregnant indigenous cow or buffalo. 

The scheme specifically focuses on indigenous breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, and Tharparkar for cows and Murrah for buffaloes. 

Eligible families can receive a financial assistance of ₹900 per month for a maximum period of six months during the gestation period of the animal. 

This translates to a total assistance of ₹5,400 for each eligible cow or buffalo. 

The financial support is intended to cover the costs of fodder, feed, and other necessary maintenance expenses for the pregnant animals. 

The application process for this scheme requires eligible families to fill out a specific application form. 

The application form can be obtained from the local animal husbandry department offices or downloaded from the official government website. 

Along with the application form, applicants must submit documents proving their BPL status. 

This includes a BPL certificate issued by the local authorities. 

Additionally, proof of ownership of the pregnant indigenous cow or buffalo is required. 

This can be in the form of a registration certificate or any other official document indicating ownership. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the local animal husbandry department officials. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

After successful verification, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

The disbursement is done on a monthly basis for the duration of six months. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the local animal husbandry department offices. 

They can also reach out to the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying through their official helpline numbers. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote indigenous livestock and improve the livelihoods of marginalized communities. 

It is expected to benefit thousands of families across the country. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2021-2022. 

This funding is aimed at ensuring that the scheme reaches its intended beneficiaries effectively. 

The scheme also aligns with the government's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and animal husbandry practices. 

By supporting indigenous breeds, the scheme aims to enhance the genetic diversity of livestock in India. 

The government anticipates that this will lead to improved milk production and better income for the families involved. 

The scheme is also expected to have a positive impact on the overall health of the livestock population. 

By providing adequate nutrition during the gestation period, the scheme aims to reduce the mortality rates of calves. 

This is crucial for maintaining the population of indigenous breeds which are often more resilient to local climatic conditions. 

The scheme is monitored regularly to ensure that the funds are utilized effectively. 

Periodic audits and assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact of the scheme on the beneficiaries. 

Feedback from the beneficiaries is also collected to make necessary improvements to the scheme. 

The government encourages beneficiaries to share their experiences and suggestions for better implementation. 

The Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme is a significant step towards supporting the SC community. 

It recognizes the importance of livestock in the livelihoods of rural families. 

By focusing on pregnant animals, the scheme ensures that the next generation of livestock is healthy and productive. 

This is vital for the economic stability of BPL families who rely on agriculture and animal husbandry for their income. 

The scheme also promotes the use of traditional farming practices that are sustainable and environmentally friendly. 

In conclusion, the Maintenance of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme for BPL Families Belonging to Scheduled Caste Category is a comprehensive welfare initiative. 

It provides financial assistance to support the maintenance of pregnant indigenous livestock. 

The scheme aims to empower marginalized communities while promoting the welfare of indigenous breeds. 

With a structured application process and clear eligibility criteria, the scheme is designed to be accessible to its intended beneficiaries. 

The government remains committed to the success of this scheme and its positive impact on the lives of BPL families.
